open_points.subject: classification of a caught per-file limit error
open_points.text: the runner ignores the signal the host sends for a write past it, so the write fails with an error the code can see ... Only that error is a scratch hit
open_points.question: If `run` catches the write error and returns conforming outputs, must the execution still be `resource_exhausted`; if so, how does `module:sandbox` observe the caught error when the signal is ignored and no hit-reporting mechanism is named?
options: Classify `resource_exhausted` even when caught, requiring a named reporting mechanism
Treat it as a scratch hit only when the error escapes `run`
Allow a caught error followed by conforming output to succeed
open_points.default_guess: Treat the error as a scratch hit only when it escapes `run`, because that is the only specified observable case.

open_points.subject: host-storage exhaustion before or outside user code
open_points.text: a write that fails because host storage is exhausted is an ordinary raised error (`crashed` if it escapes `run`)
open_points.question: What outcome applies when host-storage exhaustion prevents sandbox setup, input staging, runner communication or output collection rather than raising inside `run`?
options: Apply a phase-specific outcome, including start failure during the probe
open_points.default_guess: Treat exhaustion outside `run` as `internal_error` and stop the kernel; if it occurs during the start probe, refuse startup.
